summary: Whether allowed requests (HTTP and protocol-relay commands) are written to the egress log, for each way an operator can spell or omit it. The host copies the raw logging block into proxy-config.yaml without filling defaults in, so an omitted key runs at the EGRESS fallback while the host validates and documents its own. The two must be the same value.

implementations.host: rust/agentcage-core/src/config/parse.rs (the resolved value) and rust/agentcage-state/src/derived.rs (PROXY_KEYS: what reaches proxy-config.yaml)

fields.cage: the logging keys of a cage.yaml, merged into an otherwise minimal valid config
fields.proxy_config: the same keys as the host writes them into proxy-config.yaml; the split point, so neither half needs the other
fields.allowed_requests: whether allowed requests are logged, on both sides

notes: The host half asserts cage -> allowed_requests (its parse) and cage -> proxy_config (its writer); the proxy half asserts proxy_config -> allowed_requests (its loader). A key the host strips from proxy-config.yaml shows up as a proxy_config mismatch on the host half.

cases.why: no logging block at all, the common case: the host documents false, and the egress used to fall back to true, logging every allowed request and IMAP/SMTP command for an operator who never asked
a logging block that sets other keys only; the omitted key still resolves to the default
the documented way to opt in
the legacy top-level key is honoured when logging.allowed_requests is absent; the host stripped it from proxy-config.yaml, so it only worked by accident of the old egress fallback
the legacy key set to false: the host honoured it, the egress never saw it and logged everything
logging.allowed_requests wins whenever it is present, even as false
the same precedence the other way round
a logging block without allowed_requests does not hide the legacy key
